summary: This RFC defines algorithm names and parameters for using some SHA-2 hash algorithms for data integrity verification in SSH. It updates RFC 4253 by adding a new recommended integrity algorithm.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6668 adds two SHA-2 based HMAC algorithms for checking SSH data integrity. It recommends HMAC-SHA2-256 and makes HMAC-SHA2-512 optional.

subtitle: SHA-2 based message authentication algorithms for SSH data integrity checks.

tldr.problem: SSH users and implementers requested SHA-2 based data-integrity algorithms in addition to the previously defined SHA-1 and MD5 choices.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers HMAC-SHA2-256 as RECOMMENDED and HMAC-SHA2-512 as OPTIONAL for SSH message integrity verification.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4253 is updated with a new recommended integrity algorithm, and implementations can negotiate the added algorithm names.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 6668's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC updates RFC 4253 with SHA-2 based SSH integrity algorithms.

sections.title: Adding SHA-2 Integrity Algorithms
sections.content:
SSH's transport protocol already defined data integrity verification using SHA-1 and MD5. The RFC says users and implementers requested support for SHA-2 family algorithms because of security concerns with those earlier hash algorithms.

This document defines names and parameters for SHA-2 HMAC algorithms and updates RFC 4253 by specifying a new recommended integrity algorithm.
sections.plainLanguage: SSH peers can use an integrity check to detect altered messages. This RFC adds choices based on the SHA-2 family of hash algorithms.

sections.title: The Two HMAC-SHA2 Choices
sections.content:
hmac-sha2-256 is RECOMMENDED and uses a 32-byte digest and 32-byte key. hmac-sha2-512 is OPTIONAL and uses a 64-byte digest and 64-byte key.

Clients and servers can place these algorithm names in their proposals so the peers can negotiate an integrity method. The RFC also notes that test vectors for HMAC with SHA-2 are available in the cited reference.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC gives SSH two named SHA-2 HMAC choices, with one recommended and one optional. The peers use their algorithm proposals to agree on a choice.

sections.title: Security Notes
sections.content:
The security considerations of the SSH transport specification also apply to these algorithms. The RFC cites NIST publications that give HMAC-SHA1 and HMAC-SHA2-256 security strengths of 128 bits and 256 bits, respectively.

This document adds integrity algorithm choices; it does not change SSH's overall transport design.
sections.plainLanguage: The new choices follow SSH's existing integrity mechanism. The RFC provides security-strength information for HMAC-SHA1 and HMAC-SHA2-256.
